The **Standard: ≥90 %** is the national quality target used in the Danish healthcare system to evaluate the treatment coverage of [[antikoagulationsbehandling]] for patients diagnosed with [[atrieflimren]] [^src1] [^src2]. Managed under the Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram (RKKP), this threshold defines the minimum acceptable performance for hospitals and regions regarding specific clinical quality indicators [^src1]. 

Specifically, the ≥90% standard serves as the primary target for [[indikator-4a|Indikator 4a]], which measures the 2-year treatment coverage, and also applies to [[indikator-4a3|Indikator 4a3]], which tracks the 5-year treatment coverage [^src1] [^src2]. By setting this benchmark, the RKKP aims to monitor and improve cardiovascular care, particularly in the prevention of strokes among atrial fibrillation patients across the country [^src2].

When evaluating regional performance against this standard, the data reveals significant disparities in compliance. For instance, in a 5-year analysis, [[region-nordjylland|Region Nordjylland]] was identified as the only region in Denmark that successfully met the ≥90% standard, achieving a treatment coverage rate of 92.4% (95% CI: 89.8–94.5) [^src1]. Other regions and hospitals are continually measured against this exact threshold to determine their adherence to national healthcare quality goals and to identify areas requiring clinical improvement [^src1] [^src2].
